relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: In isolated spinal cords, capsaicin evoked concentration-dependent spinal CGRP release without compromising viability, and clinically used analgesics inhibited it, validating the assay.

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Selective Nav1.8 inhibition with suzetrigine reduced spinal CGRP release only when applied to the DRG or nerve root, not the spinal cord, indicating that Nav1.8 regulates peripheral action potential propagation rather than presynaptic transmitter release.

key_findings: In an intact human DRG-spinal cord preparation, capsaicin applied to DRG triggered CGRP release exclusively in the spinal cord.
Suzetrigine reduced spinal CGRP release only when applied to DRG or nerve root, not spinal cord, so Nav1.8 inhibitor efficacy is unlikely to improve with better CNS penetration.
